newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Karachi bourse to resist regulatory agency orders.
newsitem.headline: Karachi bourse to resist regulatory agency orders.

text.p: Pakistan's main Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) said on Friday it would resist directives from the state Corporate Law Authority (CLA) for the restructuring of its board of directors.

"The CLA wants government-nominated chief executives at the stock exchange and four directors in the board. If this happens, independence of the stock exchange will be compromised," KSE President Arif Habib told reporters.
On June 12, the CLA told KSE to change the composition of its board to bring in professionals uninvolved in the equity market.

A CLA directive said the governing boards of the directors of the stock exchanges should be restructured to allow at least 33 percent outside non-broker members representing public interests to be nominated by the CLA.

Habib said the KSE would plead its case before Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz and the CLA, adding: "If nothing comes out of it, then we will go to the court. But it would be our last option."
He said the appointment of the chief executive and board members by the government would lead to political interference in the stock market.
"Many institutions were destroyed because of political appointments as it paves the way for corruption and interference," he said. "We don't want this to happen to the KSE."
Such a step would amount to nationalising the stock market, which would be against the government's own policy of deregulation, he said.
"We have already two non-broker members in our board who are represented by the NIT (National Investment Trust) and ICP (Investment Corporation of Pakistan)," Habib said.
"...those powers which the CLA wants with the chief executive are available with KSE's general manager."
Habib said the CLA already had all regulatory powers and the stock exchanges' rules could become effective without CLA approval. The authority could also amend these rules.
"But there have been no complaints against us, the exchange has had always guarded investors' interest," he said.
In another development, a CLA official said on Friday that the authority had asked the KSE to provide details of transactions by a defaulting broker, M. Rashid Jamal.
He said the CLA had written to the KSE on Thursday asking it for details of deals in which Jamal's MRJ Securities had sold shares short or bought shares but did not collect them.
The CLA also asked the KSE for a breakdown of all claims by investors, excluding KSE members, against Jamal and how the bourse proposed to settle them.
Stocks analysts say the CLA is keen to crack down on underlying regulatory problems at the Karachi Stock Exchange.
On Wednesday, the CLA barred stock broker Zafar Moti from the Karachi and Lahore bourses for alleged trading law violations.
